title: Baked Macaroni and Cheese

items.raw: ½ teaspoon paprika, pinch of cayenne
4 ounces Gruyère or Monterey Jack, grated (about 1 cup)

steps.text: Set it to 375°F and butter a 9×13-inch baking dish.
Boil the pasta in well-salted water for 2 minutes less than the package says. Drain and rinse briefly to stop the cooking.

Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook 2 minutes, without browning. Slowly whisk in the warm milk and cook, whisking, until it thickens enough to coat a spoon, 6 to 8 minutes. Add the mustard, paprika, cayenne, salt, and pepper.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the cheese a handful at a time until smooth. Off the heat matters — boiling cheese sauce turns grainy and oily.
Stir the pasta into the sauce. It should look too saucy; the pasta will absorb a lot in the oven. Pour into the dish.
Toss the panko with the melted butter and Parmesan and scatter it over. Bake 25 to 30 minutes, until bubbling and golden. Let stand 10 minutes before serving.

notes.label: Grate your own
notes.text: pre-shredded cheese is coated in starch to keep it from clumping, and it melts into a gritty sauce.

notes.label: Ahead of time
notes.text: assemble without the topping up to a day ahead. Add the topping and bake 40 minutes, covered for the first 15.

notes.label: Stovetop version
notes.text: skip the baking and serve straight from the pot, loosened with a little milk.

notes.label: Add-ins
notes.text: crumbled bacon, caramelized onions, or a spoonful of Dijon in the sauce.

openQuestion: Whose mac and cheese is this, and when does it get made — holidays, kids’ dinners, a side at Thanksgiving? What cheeses go in, and does it have a crumb topping?
